Actionable Volume Potential
0
KLPM worth pursuing 💡Actionable Volume Potential is the estimated incremental volume worth pursuing across HPCL outlets in scope. It combines two components while avoiding double counting:

Own Recovery Potential — credible volume that can be recovered based on each outlet's own proven historical performance (current run-rate against its best sustained 12-month run-rate).

Market Capture Potential — additional credible volume arising from the current Trading Area, competitive position and comparable outlet performance: unclaimed trading-area growth, HPCL share lost in the TA, volume measurably migrated to nearby competitors, the gap to comparable HPCL outlets, and under-indexing against the market leader.

These signals overlap heavily, so they are never summed. They are ranked and combined with sharply diminishing weights, damped by competitive pressure and diagnostic confidence, capped against current throughput and unheld trading-area volume, and finally netted against the recovery component before the two are added.

This is an evidence-based actionable opportunity, not a theoretical maximum or aspirational target. No component assumes full share capture, full competitor volume, market-leader parity, or that the best-performing outlet is immediately achievable.

Expected Recovery

KLPM if actions land 💡Expected Volume Recovery is sized by the AI Decision Engine per product (MS and HSD separately) and summed. It is not the same measure as Actionable Volume Potential.

Actionable Volume Potential answers how much volume is worth pursuing at this outlet. Expected Volume Recovery answers the narrower question how much of that is likely to land from the one action being recommended this cycle — so it is always the smaller number.

Recoverable base = gap to the best sustained 12-month run-rate + recoverable competitive leakage + unclaimed trading-area growth. That base is multiplied by the action effectiveness factor, a market multiplier and the engine's confidence in its own diagnosis.

Only products the engine judges weak contribute. Effectiveness factors are conservative planning assumptions, not forecasts:
Immediate Visit 55% · Fleet Visit 45% · Win-Back Campaign 45% · Dealer Meeting 40% · Customer Acquisition 35% · Engineering 35% · Marketing 30% · CSA 25% · Competitor Intelligence 20% · Monitoring 5%.

📐 Measurement Rule
Market Share is reported at Trading Area level only. Uploaded data is outlet-level and a Trading Area is the smallest geography where the HPCL / IOC / BPCL outlet set is complete, so shares roll up accurately here and nowhere else. Region, District and Sales Area are therefore measured on Volume, Growth, Outlet Count, Actionable Volume Potential, Opportunity Volume, Priority Count and Action Count instead.
🏢 OMC Competitive Summary
▶ OMC Volume, Growth & Trading Area Leadership 💡Market Share here is share of volume, not share of a delineated market. It is each OMC's volume divided by the total volume of every outlet in the current filter — so it moves with Region, District, Sales Area, Trading Area and month selection.

The Trading Area rule below still stands: only a TA has a complete outlet set, so only TA-level share is a true market share. Read these three columns as volume mix and its movement.

Share Gain/Loss = Current Share − Historical Share, in percentage points.

TAs Led counts the Trading Areas where each OMC holds the highest volume. That is a valid aggregate because leadership is decided inside each TA, then counted.

📌 Monthly Management Focus

    ⚙️ Priority Score Engine
    ▶ 📘 How the scores are built

    Territory Priority Score

    Market Size — 20%
    Opportunity Potential — 25%
    Gap to Leader — 40%
    Growth Trend — 5%
    Strategic Position — 10%
    Total = 100

    Outlet Priority Score

    Decline Severity — 30%
    Outlet Size — 25%
    Actionable Volume Potential — 20%
    Territory Importance — 15%
    Competitive Pressure — 10%
    Total = 100

    Priority Bands

    Critical Territory ≥ 60 · Outlet ≥ 65
    High Territory 45–59 · Outlet 50–64
    Medium Territory 30–44 · Outlet 35–49
    Low below Medium

    Territory Categories

    Position — where HPCL stands today
    Attack: Leader ≠ HPCL, gap < 10%
    Develop: Leader ≠ HPCL, gap ≥ 10%, share ≥ 20%
    Expand: HPCL share < 20%
    Defend: HPCL leads, gap to #2 < 5%
    Maintain: HPCL leads, gap to #2 ≥ 5%

    Momentum — where that position is heading
    🔴 Elevated Risk: leadership lost this period, or share down ≥ 8 pp, or leading on a thin (< 8 pp) lead while share falls
    🟠 Watch: share down 3–8 pp, or share falling with competitor volume rising against a material HPCL volume decline
    🟢 Stable: everything else
    — n/a: no prior-year comparison period, so trajectory is not assessed
    Position and Momentum are independent. A comfortable leader can be deteriorating; a distant challenger can be gaining.
